reader.requirement: At --std 85 a comma or semicolon immediately followed by a space is a separator that may stand anywhere the separator space may stand (except a comma inside a PICTURE character-string, which is a picture symbol), and a comma or semicolon with no space after it is no separator.
reader.edition-search: Read SeparatorRule.cs whole (remarks: edition-invariant), the FNARG_SEPARATOR/COMMA/SEMICOLON lexer rules and the list-region actions (OnDefaultLParen, OpenRegion, OnDefaultRParen), and the subscriptList / functionArgList parser rules; grepped Edition|Version|Std in SeparatorRule.cs (none). Frontend.cs#LexAndParse passes the edition only to retypes.PrimeLexer and the debugging-line rewriter.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: w73a_separator_context_conforming covers comma/semicolon between MOVE receivers and DISPLAY operands; nothing exercises a comma separator inside a subscript, reference-modifier or function-argument parenthesis other than between two items

reader.notes: Outside parentheses that open a list region, the comma-space is skipped exactly as a space is and SR2 holds everywhere probed. Inside a REF_LPAREN or FNARG_LPAREN region (subscripts, reference modifiers, function arguments, and any grouping parenthesis nested in them) the lexer keeps ', '/'; ' as a real FNARG_SEPARATOR token, and the grammar admits that token only between two list items, so a comma or semicolon separator in any other separator-space position inside the region is a parse error.
